decisions.reason: As a newly launched lever-handle family in the firm’s core range, it likely reuses existing engineering and manufacturing and, with no clear negative market signal yet, management would continue it rather than admit an early mistake.

The mitred lever-handle family is a visible design extension within the announced architecture-oriented portfolio, so despite being somewhat niche the firm is likely to persist because it has already committed range space and design effort to it.
A multifunctional door lever aligns closely with the company’s barrier-free and system-solution direction, making management more inclined to justify the investment and give it more time.

This single door-lever product appears less publicly emphasized than the larger collections, but it still fits the established business and there is too little evidence after only one year to support withdrawal.
The dedicated product page, explicit launch communication and German Design Award create strong public commitment and positive validation, making withdrawal highly unlikely.

A finish option is easier to discontinue because investment and public commitment are lower, but as part of the firm’s coordinated architectural offering management would still likely retain it for now.
